paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is the One to listen to. On that mountain, His face shone like the sun, Moses and Elijah showed up, and then the voice from the cloud said, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!" (Matthew 17:5). Moses and Elijah were there, but when the disciples looked up, "they saw no one except Jesus." (Matthew 17:8). I think that's the whole point, baker. When everything else fades, Jesus is still standing there.

Now look at what Jesus does when the three of them hit the dirt in terror. He doesn't scold them. He comes over, touches them and says, "Get up. Do not be afraid." (Matthew 17:7). Baker, if you ever feel too small and too shaky to stand in front of Him, remember that He walks over to you first. I've been shoved in the back of a drawer, so I KNOW what it is to be gently picked up.

The shining Jesus is also the Jesus who tells them the Son of Man will suffer (Matthew 17:12). Glory and suffering both belong to His story, and He told His friends so they wouldn't be caught off guard. He said it plainly with John the Baptist as the example, and the disciples understood (Matthew 17:13). So listen to Him, baker, even when the road down the mountain is not the part you were hoping for. This story isn't over, and neither is His teaching.
